TONY SERRA TO REPRESENT STEVE KUBBY

J. Tony Serra, the charismatic trial attorney based on San Francisco's waterfront, has agreed to represent former Libertarian gubernatorial candidate, Steve Kubby in what many believe will be the defining court case in the escalating legal confrontation between police and patients over medical marijuana rights.

Serra, who is widely acknowledged as one of the country's top trial attorneys, was portrayed by actor James Wood in the 1989 HBO movie, " True Believer. " Serra said he looks forward to the Placer County case because Bay Area prosecutors aren't as aggressive in pot cases.


" The Bay Area is very tolerant, and they won't prosecute anything, " he said. " If this had been in the Bay Area, this probably would have washed out before the trial. "

Steve and Michele Kubby are scheduled to appear before a judge on Monday, February 14th at 1 PM at the Old Auburn Courthouse. Steve Kubby will request that Tony Serra be substituted for his present attorney, Dale Wood.


Kubby said that the move to bring in Serra was in response to the thousands of pages of discovery that have been dumped on his attorneys by Placer District Attorney Bradford Fenocchio and the two deputy prosecutors Gene Geni and Christopher Cattran, who are assigned to this case. Both of Kubby's attorneys have complained that they have never seen so much meaningless discovery in a case before. " It's out of control, " said Joe Farina, who will continue to represent Michele Kubby.

" I'm sorry to be losing Dale, because he has done such an outstanding job for us, " said Steve Kubby who added, " Everything Dale has predicted has come to pass. " Kubby said he was forced to recognize that the prosecutors have been burying them in documents and that they needed a larger law firm to represent them.

" Tony Serra's firm has the manpower, experience and cunning to deal with the aggressive tactics of Placer County and to secure our rights for all medical marijuana patients, " said Kubby.

Kubby said neither he nor his attorneys have seen any documents or evidence that proves he or his wife committed a single crime. " The prosecution's entire case is a stack of cards that will come crashing down on them in trial, " predicted Kubby.
